Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production change with no tests, fewer than 5 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/transcript_quotes.py
  tests/test_quote_fidelity.py
  tests/test_transcript_quotes.py

TWO DEFECTS, both measured on the real episode transcript. These lines are consecutive and all spoken by the Guest:

  line  90 [00:10:27] Guest: years into my career and by all metrics from the outside it looked like success like it I had a
  ...
  line 112 [00:11:57] Guest: into like months and years. So there was a sense of monotony. So I talk about silent burnout quite
  line 113 [00:12:05] Guest: a bit, because if you look at the research that just came out on optometry burnout for US
  line 114 [00:12:11] Guest: optometrists, it was 54%. I mean, that's every other optometrist listening in right now,

extract_quote_candidates currently returns:
  {"timestamp_s": 627.0 (10:27), "text": "I talk about silent burnout quite a bit, because if you look at the research that just came out on optometry burnout for"}

DEFECT 1 — WRONG TIMESTAMP. The quote's words are spoken at 11:57-12:11, but it is labelled 10:27, the start of the merged Guest block. The guest talks continuously from 10:27, so every sentence in that long run inherits the block's opening timestamp. A listener clicking the show-notes timestamp waits about ninety seconds to hear the quote. Show-notes timestamps must point at the words.

DEFECT 2 — TRUNCATED QUOTE. The text stops at "...on optometry burnout for" and drops "US optometrists, it was 54%", which is the entire payload of the sentence. The full sentence is "So I talk about silent burnout quite a bit, because if you look at the research that just came out on optometry burnout for US optometrists, it was 54%." A truncated quote is worse than no quote: it reads as a fabrication and loses the number that made it worth quoting.

THE FIX:
1. Carry per-line provenance through the merge. When consecutive same-speaker lines are joined, record each source line's character offset in the joined text along with that line's timestamp. Then assign every extracted SENTENCE the timestamp of the line where that sentence STARTS, not the block's opening timestamp. Add a helper (e.g. timestamp_for_offset(offsets, index)) and keep it pure so it is directly testable.
2. NEVER truncate a candidate. Cleaning may strip a leading discourse marker ("So ", "And ", "Well, ") and surrounding whitespace, but it must not remove trailing words. If a sentence exceeds MAX_QUOTE_WORDS it is REJECTED as a candidate, not shortened. Add an internal assertion or explicit check that the returned text is a contiguous substring of the joined source text after only leading-marker and whitespace normalisation, so silent word loss is structurally impossible.
3. A sentence that reaches the end of the available transcript without terminal punctuation is INCOMPLETE: reject it rather than returning a fragment. Only return sentences that end in . ! or ? (the last line of a transcript often ends mid-thought).

TESTS (tests/test_quote_fidelity.py; at least 5). Paste the four real transcript lines above as the fixture, with enough surrounding context that the Guest block genuinely starts at 10:27:
 (1) the 54% sentence is returned COMPLETE, ending with "54%." — assert the exact substring "it was 54%" is present;
 (2) that quote's timestamp_s corresponds to 11:57 or 12:05 (the lines the sentence spans), NOT 627.0 (10:27) — assert it is >= 717 and <= 731, and explicitly assert it != 627.0;
 (3) NEGATIVE: no returned candidate's text is a strict prefix of a longer sentence present in the source — i.e. nothing was truncated. Implement this as a real scan over the source text, not a hand-picked case;
 (4) NEGATIVE: a sentence longer than MAX_QUOTE_WORDS is absent from the results entirely rather than appearing shortened;
 (5) NEGATIVE: a trailing fragment with no terminal punctuation at the very end of the transcript is not returned;
 (6) every returned candidate's text appears verbatim (after whitespace collapse and leading-marker strip) inside the source transcript — the anti-fabrication check;
 (7) determinism unchanged: two calls give identical output.
Keep tests/test_transcript_quotes.py green; if an assertion pinned the block-start timestamp, UPDATE it with a one-line comment citing this defect.
